title: C Y P two C nineteen, clopidogrel, and proton pump inhibitors

segs.text: Section twelve. C Y P two C nineteen. This liver enzyme metabolizes slightly acidic drugs: proton pump inhibitors, which lower stomach acid, and also fluoxetine, sertraline and diazepam. Patients are grouped by how much of the enzyme's activity they have, from poor metabolizers, with the least, through intermediate and extensive, to ultrarapid.

Two variants, star two and star three, are single base changes that create a premature stop codon. The protein stops too early, is too short to work, and no active enzyme is made. A third variant, star seventeen, does the opposite. Its change sits in the upstream region of the gene, where the machinery that expresses the gene binds. More enzyme is made, so activity rises. Star seventeen does not change the enzyme's shape, and it is not extra gene copies.

Clopidogrel, a drug that stops platelets from sticking together, is a prodrug: C Y P two C nineteen helps turn it into its active form. So both directions cause harm. A star two or star three carrier makes too little active drug, and the platelets stay sticky. That is therapeutic failure. A star seventeen carrier makes too much active drug and is over anticoagulated. She said, clopidogrel is a drug for which we should be genotyping people for their two C nineteen status.

With proton pump inhibitors, being a poor metabolizer helps. C Y P two C nineteen clears these drugs, so low activity keeps the drug level higher. A higher level suppresses more acid, raises the stomach p H, and gives a better cure rate. This is safe because these drugs have a very wide therapeutic index. A two thousand four study by Furuta and colleagues gave lansoprazole and plotted three panels by phenotype: the total drug exposure, called area under the curve, the stomach p H over twenty four hours, and the cure rate. Poor metabolizers had the highest of all three.

The assigned reading is a different paper, Furuta and colleagues, nineteen ninety eight. Patients took omeprazole, a proton pump inhibitor, plus the antibiotic amoxicillin to cure H pylori, a stomach infection. The less C Y P two C nineteen activity a patient had, the higher the cure rate. Rapid metabolizers were cured twenty eight point six percent of the time, intermediate metabolizers sixty percent, and poor metabolizers, who make no active enzyme, one hundred percent. Poor metabolizers on a proton pump inhibitor also had more ulcer healing.

The same high levels cause harm with the other substrates. A poor metabolizer on a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, such as fluoxetine or sertraline, or on diazepam, has more adverse drug responses, including more sedation with diazepam. The poor metabolizer benefits only when the drug's therapeutic index is wide.
